subject: Request: regional rampdown/fallback impact — evidence pull and remedy options
messages:
From: Evan Lowe <evan.lowe@blueharbor.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent 503s and fallback during peak window — need confirmation for SLA

Hi Vanessa,

We saw a fairly large spike of 503 responses and elevated tail latency on 2028-03-10 between 17:42 - 18:08 PDT (US-WEST2). Our payment processing queue showed retries and a handful of failed requests that caused backoff in our pipeline. We've captured sample request-ids and a screenshot of consoles errors attached.

What we observed:
- ~6% 503 rate during window (platform metrics)
- median latency jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s, 95th to ~3.2s
- trace IDs: a short list included in request-ids-sample.txt

Blue Harbor's contract references 99.95% availability and latency targets at the per-route level. Our finance team is asking if this qualifies for an SLA remedy and, if so, what evidence you'll need. Please confirm the incident window on your side, whether any automatic routing/fallbacks occurred, and the next steps for a compensation request.

We'd appreciate an initial acknowledgement and ETA for evidence (raw logs, routing decisions). Attached: screenshot-503s.png, request-ids-sample.txt.

Thanks,
Evan Lowe
Head of Site Reliability
Blue Harbor Payments

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Evan Lowe <evan.lowe@blueharbor.com>
Cc: k.sr@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-11T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s and fallback during peak window — need confirmation for SLA

Hi Evan — thanks for the report and the attachments, we see the screenshots and the request-ids. Acknowledging on behalf of Redwood.

Quick next steps from our side:
1) I'll coordinate a telemetry pull for the window you listed (17:30–18:15 PDT) and ask infra to surface routing and autoscaler events.
2) Can you confirm the timezone for your timestamps (you listed PDT; we assume US-WEST2). Also confirm if the sample request IDs are representative (we'll use them to cross-reference traces).
3) We will produce a raw log bundle, an initial timeline, and an SLO-eligibility recommendation.

Cc'ing Karthik (SE) to help with contract mapping and Marissa/Jonas for evidence and root-cause. Expect an initial evidence bundle and ETA within 6 hours. If this is time-sensitive for an upcoming billing cut, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Lead, Americas
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, infra-oncall@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-11T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Intermittent 503s and fallback during peak window — evidence & SLO calc request

Jonas / infra team — forwarding Blue Harbor's note. Key asks:
- Validate whether the event between 2028-03-10T17:42:00-18:08:00 PDT (us-west2) maps to any autoscaler/routing fallback events. Customer reports 6% 503 and sustained tail latency.
- Please pull KV cache hit/miss rates, worker queue length, and scheduler events for the window.
- If routing fell back to a lower-tier model variant or preemptible pool, flag that explicitly.
- Attach an evidence bundle link and a short rationale on whether this is an "unavailable" SLO hit vs. an expected transient degradation (customer contract nuance).

I've attached a quick SLO_calc_v1.xlsx (stub) with candidate calc approaches — please update with exact token counts and the affected route(s). Vanessa: if infra recommends credit, we should surface a pro-rata figure and the paperwork path (do we route to finance or offer a one-off credit?).

Thanks — Karthik

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-11T14:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Intermittent 503s and fallback during peak window — evidence & SLO calc request

Vanessa / Karthik / Marissa — summary from infra after evidence pull:

What we saw
- Confirmed spike window: 2028-03-10T17:40:22 - 2028-03-10T18:06:47 PDT (matches customer window within margin).
- Root cause: transient autoscaler misconfiguration plus an aggressive routing fallback policy. During a short scaling event in us-west2, a subset of requests were routed to a lower-memory model variant (quantized) which increased latency and introduced a small 503 rate when the variant's worker pool hit connection limits.
- Metrics: 5.9% 503s across the affected route, median latency spike to ~1.05s, p95 ~3.1s. KV-cache hit rate dropped 18% during the window.

Evidence produced
- Raw log bundle (compressed): raw-log-bundle-us-west2-20280310.tar.gz (uploaded) — Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/raw-log-bundle-us-west2-20280310
- Autoscaler event trace and routing decision log: included in the bundle (file: autoscaler-events-20280310.ndjson)
- Cross-referenced request IDs from Blue Harbor: 18 matched traces, full traces in the bundle.

SLO eligibility assessment
- Contracted SLO (99.95% availability) applies at route-level. This incident represents a measurable availability degradation. The autoscaler-routed fallback to a lower-capacity variant is an internal policy action and does not constitute planned maintenance.
- Recommendation: eligible for a pro-rata remedy. Proposed remedy: 25% credit applied to the affected route's prorated invoice for the billing period, pending final verification of token counts and route usage. (Exact dollar will be calculated by Finance using the bundle and our SLO_calc_v1.xlsx inputs.)

Proposed next steps and timeline
1) Share raw bundle link with Evan (done) and ask them to confirm the sample request IDs they attached.
2) Infra will provide a short technical postmortem outline within 48 hours and a full postmortem in 7 business days (DOC-5873-postmortem-draft).
3) Finance to compute exact credit amount after we confirm token counts (I'll hand off to Marissa for the final finance runbook).
4) Immediate remediation: disable the aggressive fallback policy for this customer route for the next 72 hours and deploy a canary fix to autoscaler policy.

I'll prepare the short tech summary for Evan and include the Drive link and the recommended credit path.

-Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
